claim: For the finite uniform sampling model used in the number-theoretic appendix of Lomonaco and Kauffman's continuous-variable Shor algorithm, let \(C_a(N)=\#\{1\le n\le N:\gcd(a,n)=1\}\). Then exactly \[C_a(N)=\sum_{d\mid a}\mu(d)\left\lfloor\frac{N}{d}\right\rfloor.\] Consequently the printed finite lower bound \(C_a(N)/N\ge\varphi(a)/a\) for every \(N\ge a\) is false; \(a=6,N=10\) gives \(3/10<1/3\). If \(J_a(N)\) counts ordered pairs \(1\le n_1,n_2\le N\) satisfying \(\gcd(a,n_1)=\gcd(a,n_2)=\gcd(n_1,n_2)=1\), then exactly \[J_a(N)=\sum_{\substack{1\le d\le N\\(d,a)=1}}\mu(d)C_a(\lfloor N/d\rfloor)^2.\] Hence the appendix's conditional \(6/\pi^2\) lower bound is also false at finite cutoff: \(a=3,N=4\) gives \(J_a(N)/C_a(N)^2=5/9<6/\pi^2\). Its joint corollary fails as well: \(a=5,N=6\) gives \(13/36<96/(25\pi^2)\). For every fixed \(a\), however, the exact formulas recover the intended asymptotic mechanism: \[\lim_{N\to\infty}\frac{J_a(N)}{N^2}=\left(\frac{\varphi(a)}a\right)^2\prod_{p\nmid a}(1-p^{-2})=\left(\frac{\varphi(a)}a\right)^2\frac{6/\pi^2}{\prod_{p\mid a}(1-p^{-2})}.\] Thus the claimed finite-uniform probability guarantee must be replaced by exact finite-cutoff formulas; the \(\Omega((\log\log a)^{-2})\) scale is recovered only in an iterated large-cutoff regime, not uniformly for every finite \(N\ge a\).
integrity: All finite counterexamples are exact. The limiting formula is proved analytically by Möbius inversion, periodic reduced-residue density, dominated convergence using a \(d^{-2}\) majorant, and an absolutely convergent Euler product. Numerical checks are supplementary.
scientific_limitations: The correction applies to the finite uniform integer sampling model stated in the appendix. It does not establish the exact finite distribution of the continuous quantum measurement, nor does it invalidate the full algorithm. The asymptotic recovery is for fixed \(a\) as \(N\to\infty\), followed only then by any growth analysis in \(a\).
title: Exact finite-cutoff correction to the coprimality appendix of the continuous-variable Shor algorithm
